# Compare distribution {#sec-kolmogorov}

{{< include ../preamble.qmd >}}

## Concepts and intuitions {.unnumbered}

## Formal {.unnumbered}

$$
    D_n = \sup_x |F_n(x) - F(x)|
$${#eq-kolmogorov}
$$
    D_{n, m} = \sup_x |F_n(x) - D_m(x)|
$${#eq-kolmogorov-2D}


$$
    F_n(x)  = \frac{1}{n} \text{number}[x_i < x]
$${#eq-kolmogorov-fn}

## Examples {.unnumbered}

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: false
#| fig-cap: "Kolmogorov-Smirnov Test for Distribution Comparison"
#| label: fig-ks-test

# Example 1: Test if data follows a normal distribution
set.seed(123)
normal_data <- rnorm(100, mean = 0, sd = 1)

# Run Kolmogorov-Smirnov test against normal distribution
result1 <- ks.test(normal_data, "pnorm", mean = 0, sd = 1)
print("KS Test: Does data follow Normal(0, 1)?")
print(result1)

# Example 2: Test if data follows an exponential distribution
non_normal_data <- rexp(100, rate = 1)

# Run Kolmogorov-Smirnov test against exponential distribution
result2 <- ks.test(non_normal_data, "pexp", rate = 1)
print("KS Test: Does data follow Exponential(rate=1)?")
print(result2)

# Interpretation:
# If p-value > 0.05: we fail to reject the null hypothesis (data follows the specified distribution)
# If p-value < 0.05: we reject the null hypothesis (data does NOT follow the specified distribution)

# Example 3: Test if two samples come from the same distribution (two-sample KS test)
# Compare normal_data with another normal sample
normal_data_2 <- rnorm(100, mean = 0, sd = 1)

result3 <- ks.test(normal_data, normal_data_2)
print("KS Test: Do the two normal samples have the same distribution?")
print(result3)

# Compare normal_data with non_normal_data
result4 <- ks.test(normal_data, non_normal_data)
print("KS Test: Do normal and exponential samples have the same distribution?")
print(result4)

# Interpretation for two-sample test:
# If p-value > 0.05: we fail to reject the null hypothesis (the two samples have the same distribution)
# If p-value < 0.05: we reject the null hypothesis (the two samples have different distributions)
```

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: false
#| fig-cap: "Q-Q Plots for Distribution Comparison"
#| label: fig-qq-plots

# Set up 2x2 panel layout
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))

# Panel 1: Q-Q plot of normal_data against normal distribution
qqnorm(normal_data, main = "Q-Q Plot: normal_data vs Normal(0,1)")
qqline(normal_data, col = "red", lwd = 2)

# Panel 2: Q-Q plot of non_normal_data against normal distribution (should show departure)
qqnorm(non_normal_data, main = "Q-Q Plot: non_normal_data vs Normal(0,1)")
qqline(non_normal_data, col = "red", lwd = 2)

# Panel 3: Q-Q plot comparing two normal samples
qqplot(normal_data, normal_data_2, main = "Q-Q Plot: normal_data vs normal_data_2")
abline(0, 1, col = "red", lwd = 2)

# Panel 4: Q-Q plot comparing normal vs exponential samples
qqplot(normal_data, non_normal_data, main = "Q-Q Plot: normal_data vs non_normal_data")
abline(0, 1, col = "red", lwd = 2)

# Reset plot layout
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

```
